{{Quote|The stealth field generator bends light around its wearer so he can't be seen. Handy for escaping boring conversations, but there are limits.|Trymbo|<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
'''Stealth field generators''', alternatively known as '''personal stealth fields''' and '''personal cloaking devices''',<ref name="WRAITH" /> were small devices worn at the belt that hid the wearer in a manner similar to the larger [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]].<ref name="KOTORCG" />

==Characteristics==
During the [[Old Republic era]] stealth field generators were typically small and unobtrusive devices worn on the belt, consisting of emitters and a standard [[Power cell/Legends|power pack]] that could power the device for roughly five minutes. Using technology similar to [[Personal energy shield/Legends|personal energy shields]], stealth field generators emitted a [[sound-dampening field]] as well as bent light around the wearer; this made the wearer incredibly difficult to detect aurally and visually, though didn't grant total invisibility.<ref name="KOTORCG" />

By the time of the [[Rebellion era]], stealth field generators were a relic of an age long-past, and those that remained were considered antiques. Despite this, several contemporary efforts were made by various military organizations and stealth technology companies to recreate field generators with modern technology.<ref name="CORERULE" /> These modern recreations had much longer battery life, and used a combination of optical camouflage, low-output electromagnetic dampers, electronic acoustic bafflers, and thermal shielding to make a user virtually invisible to the naked eye and nearly all [[sensor]]s and [[scanner]]s. Despite their advances, however, these systems were not perfect, and did not offer total invisibility.<ref name="C&M" />

==Limitations==
Regardless of the era they were produced in, both antique and recreation stealth field generators were notoriously sensitive, with the camouflage fields prone to collapse under stress.<ref name="C&M" /><ref name="KOTORCG" /> This flaw was theorized by scientists to be an inherent limitation of the miniaturization of technology originally used in starships, among other design flaws.<ref name="CORERULE" />

Ultimately this limited stealth fields in a variety of ways; quick movements tended to destabilize the field easily, and most users could only move at a fast walk for fear of the field collapsing,<ref name="C&M" /> with it requiring skill and training to move anywhere close to a run.<ref name="KOTOR" /> Actions involving sudden outward movement, such as engaging in combat, and weapons fire across a broad spectrum of energy types was disruptive to the stealth field - taking damage or delivering it was often enough to cause a collapse.<ref name="KOTORCG" /><ref name="KOTOR" />

Further, the camouflage that stealth fields offered wasn't perfect, with many field generators creating a visual distortion or phantasmal silhouette that, while near-to impossible to see, could still be detected if the user wasn't well trained in their use.<ref name="KOTOR" /> Because of this, users of stealth fields could not move with impunity and had to be mindful of detection, often using shadows and cover to their advantage.<ref name="C&M" />

==History==
{{Quote|Stealth fields don't fool thermal detonators.|Torian Cadera|<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic" />}}
Stealth fields became prominent during and after the [[Jedi Civil War]], where they were a novel technology. During this time they were widely used by [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith Assassins]] and [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]], as well as criminal elements such as the [[GenoHaradan]] and the [[Exchange]]. Under [[Darth Malak]]'s [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], a group of researchers on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] developed a special sound dampening stealth field generator<ref name="KOTOR" />

By the time of the [[Rebellion era|Rebellion]], stealth field technology had become vanishingly rare - to the point that most governments didn't even bother to place restrictions on the technology's use.<ref name="CORERULE" /> Certain governments and intelligence organizations still made use of the technology, however, most notably [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] from the [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Bothan Spynet]],<ref name="BF2">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> [[Shadowtrooper]]s from the [[Empire Reborn]],<ref name="JediKnight">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref> and [[Imperial Saboteur]]s.<ref name="Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

Despite the decline in their use, several stealth technology companies, primarily [[Fabritech/Legends|Fabritech]] and [[Kerner (company)|Kerner Corp.]], attempted to recreate the technology through contemporary technology. These modern recreations were more advanced and power efficient than their antique counterparts, and were available for sale as restricted items.<ref name="C&M" />

==Behind the scenes==
The stealth field generator was specifically designed for the ''Knights of the Old Republic'' video game duology, although it made it first appearance in the [[2002]] game [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast|''Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast'']], with stealth fields going on to appear in numerous ''Star Wars'' video games before being introduced into the wider canon. Within games they are typically portrayed by using a frame buffer effect to show the stealthed individual as a three-dimensional transparent distortion in the air.
